items.statement: Among adults discharged alive after community-acquired pneumonia, the hazard of a first cardiovascular event in years two to five is at most 1.2 times that of matched population controls after adjustment for frailty and existing heart disease, while the first-year hazard ratio exceeds 1.5.
items.rationale: Consistent with the retrieved cohorts; separates early from late risk, which is what follow-up planning needs.
items.risks: Residual confounding by frailty; linkage not yet approved.

items.statement: Against patients admitted with other acute infections, the excess cardiovascular risk after pneumonia is small and limited to the first year.
items.rationale: Infection controls share frailty, isolating what is specific to pneumonia.
items.risks: Other infections may share cardiovascular effects.

items.statement: Adults aged 75 and over who lived alone are about twice as likely to move into a care home within two years of pneumonia as matched controls.
items.rationale: Supported by one retrieved cohort; patient-important.
items.risks: Care home entry depends on address data quality.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected with early and late windows.
